newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T says div reflects short term pain.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T says div reflects short term pain.

text.p: A surprise decision by B.A.T Industries Plc on Wednesday to hold its dividend payments was due to the cost and uncertainty of the U.S. tobacco industry's settlement of legal claims against it, said Michael Prideaux, head of public affairs.
"It's a case of short-term pain for long-term gain. The point of all this is that people will now be able to put a value on Brown and Williamson within the group," said Prideaux in an interview.
Brown & Williamson, a subsidiary of B.A.T, is the third largest cigarette maker in the United States with brands like Kent, Lucky Strike and Kool.
American tobacco companies agreed with state attorney's in June to settle most legal claims against them in return for payments totalling 230 billion pounds over 25 years.

Under the agreement, the tobacco industry has also accepted tougher regulation of their products and advertising restrictions in return for immunity from most legal claims. The funds raised by the levy will be used to meet Medicaid costs incurred for treating smoking related diseases.
If the settlement terms are approved by Congress B.A.T is obliged to pay $1.7 billion upfront. The second payment into the fund falls due one year after enactment.
Earlier B.A.T announced a maintained interim dividend of 10 pence per share and an unchanged final dividend of no less than last year's 16.0 pence.
Analysts had forecast an increase to between 10.7p and 10.8p per share at the half-year stage and a five to eight percent rise in the final dividend.
"We think it would have been misleading given the short term uncertainty to have carried on as usual," said Prideaux.
Prideaux said the proposal was under attack from health groups and the timetable for enactment was slipping.
"We were hopeful it would be enacted by the end of this year but that is now looking less likely," he said, adding there were two important motives for not letting it slip too far.

"First, the $10 billion upfront payment is not payable until the proposals are enacted. Second, the first payment into the fund is not due until the end of the first full year following enactment. So the States who stand to get most of this money for their Medicaid programmes could be waiting until 1999."

Earlier, B.A.T reported a five percent fall in its pre-tax profits to 1.247 billion stg in the six months to June 30, due mainly to the 61 million stg impact of the strength of sterling on foreign exchange markets.

The company reported a strong increase in tobacco sales in the Latin America region, supporting its rationale for the acquisition of Cigarerra La Moderna, the leading cigarette maker in Mexico, for $1.7 billion announced on July 22.

The group's Lucky Strike brand showed strong sales in Germany and Spain while total profits in Europe were 25 million higher at 86 million stg, reflecting higher cigarette prices, especially in Germany.
